I've been working this land in Quzhou for decades. I know this county — the soil, the water table, the seasons. Let me think through what I'll do this year.

My 20 mu needs to work hard. The wheat-maize rotation is the backbone — I'll put 14 mu into that double-cropping system, which gives me two harvests off the same ground. The remaining 6 mu goes to cotton, as it has most years. Cotton prices have been reasonable, and I know how to grow it here.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll plant in early October. I've switched to improved semi-dwarf varieties over the years — they lodge less and yield better. I'll plough that ground after the maize comes off, then apply base fertilizer before seeding. I irrigate at sowing, jointing, heading, and grain fill — four times. That's how you get 500 kg/mu here. Aphids and powdery mildew are my main worries, so two pesticide passes minimum.

**Maize (summer):** Straight into the stubble after wheat harvest in June — I'll use rotary tillage to chop the straw and prepare the bed. Hybrid seed, no question. Summer rains help, but the well gives me insurance for 2 irrigations. Corn borer and armyworm I'll watch closely.

**Cotton (spring):** I'll plough and ridge the cotton plot in late March. Bt hybrid cotton — I've used it for years, cuts my pesticide burden on bollworm considerably. Still need to spray for aphids and spider mites though, so I'll plan four applications. Cotton drinks water during boll setting — I'll irrigate four times with the well.

With some family off-farm, I have less labor, so I lean on machinery and no-till where I can on the maize.
